# B494 row (h): SIGTERM mid-guest, and guest traps with the Go runtime's signal handlers installed
confined: yes (pods below; uid 250, sandboxed=1 self-reported in the b494-hello/jit runs of the same image); profile file not readable without sudo.
Timing sources: 'delete issued' and 'gone' are host UTC stamps from the driver (gone = first failing 'ps -p <pid>' poll, 50 ms);
SIGNAL lines are the process's own stamps (crilog via kubectl logs -f); 'graceful-stop outcome' is the node agent's log line (local time, UTC-4).
The pod object is force-deleted by the provider after teardown, so status/exit code is not readable afterwards; the agent line's
escalated=false|true is the record of whether SIGKILL was needed.

## 1. epoch interruption on SIGTERM (the design), terminationGracePeriodSeconds=30
pod b494-spin-epoch2 uid=30e014e4-6fe0-4cca-aa84-b78f0541c688 terminationGracePeriodSeconds=30 command=["/bin/wasmspike","spin","@wasm/spin.wasm"]

2026-10-15T04:35:05.134890000Z B494 2026-10-15T04:35:05.134385Z +5529ms SIGNAL terminated received; engine.IncrementEpoch()
container "spike" in pod "b494-spin-epoch2" is not available=> SIGTERM reached the process 0.198 s after the delete; the process left 1.533 s after SIGTERM (the 1.5 s is the deliberate
   log-drain pause after the trap); escalated=false: no SIGKILL. Exit well inside the 30 s grace.

container "spike" in pod "b494-spin-ignore2" is not available=> without epoch interruption a spinning guest ignores SIGTERM; the node escalated to SIGKILL at the grace end (8.08 s after SIGTERM,
   escalated=true). Epoch interruption is what turns SIGTERM into a guest stop; the grace bound holds either way.

## 3. the trap the SIGTERM path produces (same binary, host process, kill -TERM; the in-pod stream closes on deletion before this line)
B494 2026-10-15T04:35:44.451077Z +5ms guest spin entered (epoch=true)
B494 2026-10-15T04:35:45.475130Z +1029ms SIGNAL terminated received; engine.IncrementEpoch()
B494 2026-10-15T04:35:45.475730Z +1029ms RESULT guest stopped: trap code=10(Interrupt) last="wasm trap: interrupt"; exiting 143 in 1.5s (the pause only lets the log stream drain)

=> unreachable, integer divide by zero and an out-of-bounds load each come back as a *wasmtime.Trap with its code, under both
   wasmtime's default macOS Mach-port exception handling and Config.SetMacOSUseMachPorts(false) (Unix signal handlers).
   Go's own SIGSEGV handling works before and after (a Go nil dereference is recovered as a runtime panic). No crash, exit 0.
